subject: Pilot charter & kickoff handoff — HelioTech (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@heliotech.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@heliotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot charter & kickoff handoff — HelioTech (post-discovery)

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the proposed pilot (POC) that we recommend to validate the integration and value you outlined. Please review and confirm next steps.

Top-level pain / goals we heard
- Inconsistent accuracy on document extraction and summarization for technical manuals (primary pain).
- Peak inference latency needs to be <200ms for interactive support flows.
- Unit cost must stay below target thresholds to make productization viable.

Proposed pilot scope (2–4 weeks)
- Objective: Demonstrate 80% classification accuracy on the 3-source manual corpus and median token latency <200ms for interactive queries.
- Workstreams:
  1) Integration: API + S3 ingestion to host a 5k-doc prompt set for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
  2) Eval: Prompt suite (sample prompts attached) and automated eval harness to measure accuracy, latency, and token usage.
  3) Ops/Cost: Baseline run to measure per-token cost and recommend batching/quantization profile.

Success metrics (mutually agreed)
- Accuracy: >=80% on labeled prompt set (precision-weighted).
- Latency: median end-to-end generation latency <200ms (95th <400ms).
- Cost: projected per-1000-query cost under $3 after suggested optimizations.
- Stakeholder sign-off on one sample workflow end-to-end.

Owners & core contacts
- Redwood AE (commercial): Soojin Lee — soojin.lee@redwood.ai (mailbox owner)
- Redwood CSM: Ben Carter — ben.carter@redwood.ai
- Redwood Solutions/Infra: Mina Haddad — mina.haddad@redwood.ai
- HelioTech PM: Alex Murphy — alex.murphy@heliotech.com
- HelioTech Data Lead: Priya Nair — priya.nair@heliotech.com

Initial timeline (target)
- Week 0 (this week): Access provisioning, data ingestion checks, pilot charter sign-off
- Week 1: Integration + initial runs on sample prompt set; baseline metrics captured
- Week 2: Iteration on prompts, quantization/batching tuning, run full eval
- Week 3: Final acceptance run, results review, and next steps for expansion or Dedicated plan

Immediate access checklist (actions for HelioTech)
- Provide an S3 bucket with read access to the pilot corpus and a service account with role to read objects.
- Allowlist Redwood egress IPs for the S3 endpoint or set up a pre-signed ingestion path.
- Create a short-lived API token for initial integration (we will rotate).
- If you prefer VPC peering for Private deployment, flag that now and we will bring infra team in.

Attachments: heliotech-pilot-charter.xlsx (charter + eval matrix), heliotech-access-checklist.pdf (access items)

Next steps / asks
- Alex / Priya: confirm agreement on the scope & success metrics and share S3 access by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4).
- Ben / Mina / Soojin: we will schedule a kickoff technical session once access is available (30–45 minutes).

Thanks — excited to get started.

—
Sooj in Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0167

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot charter & kickoff handoff — HelioTech (post-discovery)

Thanks Soojin — this looks right and appreciated the clarity. A few quick notes:

- Confirmed: Priya and I are comfortable with the 2–4 week window; we prefer tight iterations.
- Access: we'll provision a read-only S3 bucket by Wednesday; I'll add a bucket policy that allows the redwood-inference-service-account@heliotech to list/get.
- Data: we'll include a small labeled subset (about 500 docs) for the eval harness — Priya will share a link.

One ask: for the latency target, can you confirm if the 200ms target includes retrieval time or just generative token latency? We want to be explicit when we evaluate end-to-end UX.

If you can confirm that, we will sign off and hand over access.

Alex

Hi Alex / Priya — quick answers and the infra checklist (summary below). I attached a more detailed access checklist (heliotech-access-checklist.pdf) to the thread.

Latency note: our latency SLOs in the charter refer to end-to-end user-perceived time (retrieval + generation) where retrieval is a cached vector search. For clarity we'll record both retrieval and generation medians during the baseline run so you have separate numbers.

Minimal infra checklist (summary)
- S3: bucket name + ARN + service account IAM ARN (read-only) or pre-signed ingestion URL.
- Network: allowlist Redwood egress IPs (list included in attached doc) OR provide VPC peering details for private deployment.
- Samples: upload the 500-doc labeled set to s3://heliotech-pilot/samples/ with a small manifest.csv.
- API tokens: create a short-lived token for initial runs; we will exchange via our secure token flow.
- Monitoring: enable object-level logs on the bucket for 2 weeks to help debug ingestion issues.

I will be on the kickoff call to validate ingestion and run the first baseline. Proposed slots: Wed 11/04 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 11/05 09:00–09:45 PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send the invite.

—
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
